bet.text: Expect heavy defense: shoot on the move, carry a very large hopper, be extremely durable, and still fit under the trench.

demand.text: The team expected an aggressive game in which defense had a huge impact, and designed around that. It started with a level 3 climb, found it too heavy and complex for a real game, and changed to level 1 mid-season.

auto.text: Paths are drawn in the team's own planner. If it collides in the opening rush to the neutral zone, the robot can shorten its path instead of fighting for the same fuel.
A double swipe teaser in February ended at a climb that was still unfinished.
An observer calls its three-robot neutral zone sweeps in Galileo qualification 87 perfectly coordinated.

cycle.text: The intake feeds fuel into the hopper; it then goes along the roller floor, between two vertical belts and up an active ramp to the turret, which shoots while moving.
In a solo match a video analyst saw it drive circles without stopping, pass fuel back, herd it through the trench and miss a decent amount.

endgame.text: A level 1 climber on a threaded rod of 2 mm pitch, which does all the reduction.

fallback.text: Against defense the drive locks in an X, which cancels shooting on the move but empties the hopper faster and accurately. Two rear cameras cover for the turret camera.
A lost turret position is recovered manually: turned by eye, then zeroed. It worked well enough in some of the practice matches where it was needed.

gave_up.text: The level 3 climb, and some of the driver automation it had the year before.
The turret zeroes only within about ±30 degrees, and starting elsewhere broke the energy chain a few times, not at the championship.
Grounding wires to the carpet helped little against suspected static, and it lost its CANivore in Einstein match 7.

changed.text: Its own custom swerve modules with thin tread were easily pushed in training, so it swapped to MK5 with wide spiked tread mid-season.
Before the season it kept zip-tied tread because it swaps fast and wears slowly, and traction was not an issue.
A moving intake ramp became a kicker that stays open. The indexer took three or four iterations.
Off-season: drivetrain and conveyor went into a practice robot, Blitzer.

outcome.text: 47-5-0 in official play; won the Galileo division; pick 1 of the Galileo alliance on Einstein; ranked 8 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 323.27, Galileo).

functions.name: Drive base

solves.text: Not be pushed easily when defended

functions.type: SDS MK5 swerve with spiked tread

facts.text: 29.5 by 24.5 in, with the intake on the wide side
The MK5 fit almost perfectly because the old custom module had similar dimensions, and the swap took a weekend with a few tweaks to some parts
Module top plates were integrated, which also made them stronger
Spikes are kept clean and new because their condition has a massive impact on grip
MK5 gearing is R1

cost.text: The battery jumped enough in fierce practice to nearly or fully loosen its connector, until thicker foam squeezed it in place; some plates that support it bent from jumps

functions.name: Hopper

solves.text: Carry a very large amount of fuel on a robot that fits under the trench

functions.type: hopper walls of thin polycarbonate and net

facts.text: Holds about 60 fuel, by the student's estimate
The walls' flexibility maximizes capacity
Bumper padding attaches to the hopper walls, so they come off together for access
In early March, before netting, it held about 50 to 55 fuel and hardly reached that consistently, because fuel bounced out of the open top

functions.name: Intake

solves.text: Be wide and durable, collapse on impact and swap quickly when broken

functions.type: two-roller intake on a rack and gear

facts.text: Two silicone-coated rollers on an X60
Polycarbonate racks with aluminum and brass gears, made in the team's shop
A 25 x 50 mm front extrusion, and sides of two 6 mm polycarbonate and two 1.5 mm aluminum plates
The whole U-shaped frame lifts off after three screws on each side
The rollers are polycarbonate with silicone wraps

functions.name: Kicker roller

solves.text: Replace a moving ramp that was a problem when the intake opened above fuel

functions.type: passive bottom roller that drops once

facts.text: Opens once at the beginning of the match and stays there
A plain aluminum roller pulled down by surgical tubing, stowed behind the intake before the match

solves.text: Move fuel to the shooter fast without jams where the path narrows

facts.text: Active silicone-coated rollers
One X60 at two to one; 3 mm GT2 belts between rollers, chosen over 5 mm HTD for efficiency on small radii
A slight speed reduction between rollers limits jams from four balls wide to three and a half
Two rollers are slick, not silicone-coated, to cut friction
The interview calls the rollers carbon fiber; a later team post says most are polycarbonate with silicone wraps, with a few carbon fiber ones where bending could touch parts below
The floor runs at 75 rps with the belts at 95 rps for scoring, and 85 and 100 rps for passing

cost.text: Three or four iterations of ratios and belts; at the start it was really not working well

functions.name: Vertical belts
functions.type: two vertical HTD belts with separate motors

facts.text: Belts 30 mm wide on two X44 motors, surface speed
Fuel is pressed by around
Prototypes joined the belts, which worked all right; separate motors make the belts easier to remove and assemble outside
Thin PTFE sheet on polycarbonate lines the left wall and the side walls into the shooter to cut friction
Carbon fiber tubes behind the belts hold the backing plate with zip ties and serve as dead axles for pulleys, which saves shafts

functions.name: Vertical kicker roller
functions.type: powered vertical roller beside the belts

facts.text: Reuses a shooter roller from the 2024 robot, on an X44
It turns toward the belts at 60 rps; high stator current for several code cycles counts as a jam and reverses it briefly
Three rows of 2 1/4 in flexible wheels and two rows of 2 in stealth wheels on one X60
Ball speed
An opposing roller makes the ball reach the turret with zero spin
A static ramp makes balls rotate; powered wheels oppose that spin, which slightly improved the flow

functions.name: Turret shooter

solves.text: Make the turret's outer diameter as small as possible for more ball rate and fuel capacity

functions.type: compact turret with hood, nearly no spin

facts.text: The ball path is offset on an 8 in bearing so the turret sits further into the corner, leaving room for indexing
The back rollers are driven from the main shooter wheel by belts and gears, which saves weight and space
Motors sit close to the wheels in an SLS print to cut the diameter
The turret is a two-plate sandwich on the bearing; tight slots made it significantly stiffer until scraped smooth, a lesson for thin bearings
No flywheel: the wheel recovers in around 50 ms at top speed, which the team reckons is enough for 20 balls per second, way more than it needs
The feeder wheels run at 60% of shooter wheel speed, with a surface speed of at least 5 m/s
The hood's X44 drives through 1:4 in a VersaPlanetary Lite with a printed cover, then 1:19.333 in gears; the motor shaft was shortened to fit
The shooter wheel is custom, after a 4 in aluminum traction wheel worked in prototypes, and is wide enough for small feeding errors from the offset path
Flywheel feedforward is the derivative of the simulated speed function; the turret's is the target's angular rate minus the robot's

cost.text: The printed PLA hood guide was replaced quite a few times because its upper teeth kept hitting the trench, directly or through a stuck ball

functions.name: Turret energy chain

solves.text: Wire the turret and still allow a wide range of rotation

functions.type: custom printed energy chain on a narrow neck

facts.text: 14 gauge motor wires, where 12 or 10 is standard, keep the links small
The interview gives about 640 degrees of rotation and also 360 or more each way

cost.text: 14 gauge drops more voltage, which could brown out the shooter motors, so the team lowered Kp, left out a flywheel and used 10 gauge from the chain to the power distribution, with 30 A breakers

functions.name: Turret zeroing
functions.type: through-bore encoder read in a narrow window

facts.text: The encoder zeroes properly only within about 30 degrees either side
During a match the turret is turned by eye toward the intake and then zeroed on the encoder
A team member says the design could have been much better: a Hall effect sensor, used in past seasons, or two gears with the Chinese remainder theorem would fix it or at least catch a wrong start

cost.text: Starting or zeroing at another angle broke the energy chain a few times during the season, though not at the championship

functions.name: Climber

solves.text: Replace a level 3 climb that was too heavy and complex

functions.type: level 1 climber on a threaded rod

facts.text: Rod pitch
The rod does all the reduction, so the motor has none

functions.name: Shoot-on-the-move simulation

solves.text: Shoot while moving without heavy computing on the robot

functions.type: off-robot trajectory simulation fitted to polynomials

facts.text: Simulates gravity, air resistance and Magnus effect for a range of distances and robot velocities, and picks the best trajectory by cost functions for scoring or passing
The robot computes only the fitted polynomials
Robot acceleration was added this year, which improves shooting on the move against defense
Two factors are tuned by shooting near and far: exit speed against wheel speed, and the speed a ball gains as it expands; near shots are more sensitive to expansion, far shots to the speed factor
The operator can adjust exit velocity live on the dashboard, used mainly in training matches
Hood angle is taken as exit angle, since early prototypes showed a negligible difference
Defense mode puts the modules in an X and basically ignores odometry, relying on camera pose alone
A reply, written as if by a team member, says feedforward uses wanted rather than measured robot velocity for less noise, so collisions spoil it, and that most inaccuracy came with a low battery

cost.text: In Israel's solo matches it overshot and missed about 170 fuel by the team's estimate; it blames speeds raised for worn shop fuel and guesses 60 to 80 after adjusting

functions.name: Turret camera
functions.type: camera on the turret plus two rear cameras

facts.text: Runs PhotonVision on an Orange Pi; on the turret because of the number of AprilTags on the hub
Rear cameras cover blind spots and turret camera disconnects, which happened a few times
The cameras, above all the turret's, also compute a gyro offset that cancels drift, used even when no tags are seen

cost.text: For most of the season the gyro drifted, by 10 degrees in some matches and 30 in extreme cases, which threw off turret aim; disabling the Pigeon 2's no-motion calibration gave no improvement

facts.text: Lets the robot shoot while tilted on the bump

functions.name: Low battery feedback
functions.type: controller rumble and automatic conveyor slowdown

facts.text: Below a battery voltage threshold the controller rumbles, harder as voltage falls, so the driver learns how sharply to drive; touch was free while sight and sound were loaded
If the shooter wheels stay below target for a sustained period the conveyor slows so they can recover; the driver also accelerates slowly while shooting on the move

cost.text: With a battery not in perfect condition it still ended matches with brownouts

decisions.choice: Bought MK5 modules with spiked tread
decisions.because: training with the team's defense robot showed how easily its own modules were pushed, and wide spiked tread digs into the carpet; on its own tread it could only shoot against the wall and drifted too long before getting up to speed to escape
decisions.instead_of: its own custom modules with thin tread

decisions.because: trench and bump force slowing and turning, so the fast ratio's peak speed was unreachable; the slower one was much more agile
decisions.instead_of: a fast ratio chosen for long drives

decisions.because: slap-down intakes do not collapse well on impact

decisions.choice: Almost no spin on the shot
decisions.because: prototypes showed it was the most consistent with the lowest energy loss
it saves computing power on the robot

decisions.choice: Separate motors for the two vertical belts
decisions.because: they can be treated as separate modules, assembled outside and put in
decisions.instead_of: joining the belts, which worked all right in prototypes

decisions.because: silicone-coated ones could not reach Israel fast enough
the level 3 climb was too heavy and too complex to work in a real game

decisions.choice: Rigid supports and high-efficiency drives on first stages
decisions.because: friction is felt most on first stages and on fast-moving parts; anything stiff at assembly is rebuilt, though less strictly on the first robot

decisions.choice: No fuel detection or intake assist
decisions.because: it had very little value in teleop, proved little use and complex for auto, and other work came first
decisions.instead_of: a camera pipeline that steered toward fuel clusters, left unfinished

decisions.choice: Rotate the robot with the triggers
decisions.because: it frees the thumb, separates rotation from translation and makes a single driver easy; the team has done it since 2015
